cefrAlignment: Fits B2 fluency and coherence descriptors (can produce stretches of language at a fairly even tempo, uses a limited number of cohesive devices to link utterances into clear, coherent discourse). The markers and models are spoken B2 register.
examFidelity: IELTS Part 3 (no prep, 45–60 s guidance), TOEFL Take an Interview (no prep) and TOEIC Express an opinion (45 s prep, 60 s speaking) match exams.ts. The 137-word model fits 60 s.
fixes: Replaced 'Like,…' as a recommended example marker with 'A good example is…'. The lesson and checklist warn against 'like' as a filler, so recommending it was contradictory.
'TOEFL and TOEIC raters' became 'TOEFL and TOEIC speaking scores also reward a natural pace…', because TOEFL speaking is scored automatically. This matches ETS's own wording.
Changed 'video call… which wasn't really possible twenty years ago' to 'much harder', because video calling did exist in 2006.
Lengthened model answer 1 by one sentence so it is closer to the 45–60 s Part 3 length the lesson recommends.
Softened the IELTS tip from 'should be about 45–60 seconds' to 'aim for about 45–60 seconds'. It is guidance, not an official rule.
learnerOutcome: A learner can fill thinking time with natural phrases instead of silence or repeated 'um', and link a 45–60 second spoken answer with markers for adding, contrasting, examples, rephrasing and summing up.
